output.brief: Don't discipline drivers or retrain everyone. The evidence points to contaminated brake fluid from one outside garage, not driver technique, the new pads or the hilly routes. Northfield Motor Services serviced 13 Eastgate vans during the bay closure, and 11 of them are exactly the vans with soft-pedal complaints. Eleven of the 13 came from a bulk drum that had been open since March, with its cap missing at an August check. The garage's own tests found two warranty-return vans' fluid had taken on water and boiled at about 150°C, against 255°C for sealed stock. The two vans serviced from a fresh drum have no complaints. Calder Road's 12 vans, with the same pads and routes, have none either. The same drivers report nothing in other vans, including on Upper Wend. Northfield warned Larkspur on 25 Sep, and nobody replied. I'm fairly confident, about 85–90%. Next: pull all 13 Northfield vans now, test the fluid, renew it from sealed stock, and keep LK-209 parked until it is checked. Reply to Northfield, withdraw the warning plan, and tell drivers that reporting is welcome. Pad squeal is a separate, unresolved question: fresh pads are confounded, so don't change supplier yet.
